description: Renode's register DSL combinators. These are RULES, not emitter source code: the converter reads them from the database and knows nothing about any individual combinator. Adding support for a new one is a data change.

rules.name: WITH_FLAG_COMPUTED
rules.gap: computed field: needs a dispatch arm
rules.note: A callback with no `out` parameter has no storage. Emitting a field handle here would fabricate one, so the rule emits a tag and reports the gap.

rules.name: WITH_VALUE_COMPUTED
rules.gap: computed field: needs a dispatch arm

rules.name: REGISTER_CALLBACK
rules.note: Deliberately emits nothing. These carry behaviour, not register shape, and a plausible-looking guess would leave the oracle checking generated guesswork.

register_forms.name: DEFINE_EXTENSION
register_forms.note: `Register.Status.Define(this, 0xC0, name: "USART_SR")` -- the offset is the enum member passed as the first argument, which Roslyn records as a constant.

register_forms.name: DICTIONARY_ADD
register_forms.note: `{(long)Registers.Mode, new DoubleWordRegister(this).With...}` -- a dictionary initialiser, which desugars to Dictionary.Add(key, value). Offset is the key; the combinator chain is inside the value.

expressions.name: FLAG_FIELD_READ
expressions.note: `someFlag.Value`. The symbol normalises to IRegisterField<T>.Value because call targets are keyed on OriginalDefinition, so flag-vs-value is distinguished by the RESULT TYPE, not the interface name.

expressions.name: IRQ_SET
expressions.note: `IRQ.Set(x)` drives the interrupt line. The GPIO object is not modelled yet, so this assigns the peripheral's own flag.

assignments.name: FLAG_FIELD_WRITE
assignments.note: `someFlag.Value = x`. Rust has no assignable property, and D2's handles are indices, so this is a bank call rather than an lvalue -- which is why assignment needs a PROJECT rule and not just the generic `{target} = {value}`.

callback_signatures.note: The DSL's callback types. A lambda bound to one of these parameters is emitted as a free fn with this signature; `bank` and `state` are what the C# closure captured via `this`.

writeCallback.params: bank: &Bank<S>, st: &mut S, _idx: usize, _old: u64, new: u64

peripheral_methods.note: EVERY peripheral method becomes a free fn over (bank, state) -- not only the ones that touch the bank. Inside a DSL callback you hold `&Bank<S>` and `&mut S`, which is the peripheral taken apart, so a method reached from a callback cannot have a `self`. Splitting methods by whether they touch registers would give two calling conventions and a classification that shifts as rules change; 49 of 296 methods in register-bearing types touch a field today, but which ones is not a stable property. Uniform is cheaper and needs no analysis.
peripheral_methods.why_handles_in_state: The field handles must be reachable from a free fn, so they live in S alongside the peripheral's data rather than in a sibling struct the callback cannot see.

state_struct.note: The peripheral's non-register instance fields. The declared type decides: an IFlagRegisterField/IValueRegisterField/IEnumRegisterField is a HANDLE and already lives in `Fields`; anything else is real data and belongs in State. Derivable from the corpus, so State is generated rather than hand-declared -- which is what lets a callback reach `st.receive_fifo` in generated code.

also_state.note: State is not only `kind='field'`. A PROPERTY or EVENT can hold peripheral state too -- STM32_UART declares `IRQ` as a property and `CharReceived` as an event, and both were missing from a fields-only query.

type_map.note: Renode types with no BCL equivalent. `Core.GPIO` is an output line; the peripheral only ever sets its level, so `bool` carries it. Consistent with the IRQ_SET expression rule, which assigns a bool.

requires_storage.note: Only members that actually store go in State. `STM32_UART.BaudRate` computes from two register fields and holds nothing; emitting it as a field would invent storage the C# does not have -- the same error class as the invented `.with_reserved(9, 23)`. Derived from member.has_storage, so it is not a hand-maintained skip list.
